name: blender_diagnose
description: Reports the server version, whether the add-on inside Blender answers (with the Blender version and whether it is busy), the machine Blender runs on — platform, home and data directory, which is where every path in a tool call lives — how clients reach this server (stdio, or HTTP with its public address and how long file links last), the SSH tunnel to Blender when the server opens one, the project folder the client works in and its twin over there — over HTTP a note instead, since the server sees none of the client's folders — whether the add-on installed in Blender is the build this server ships and which commands it lacks if it is not, the effective configuration, the data directory, and the traffic over the link since the server started: requests, failures by type, the busiest commands with their timings, and how much of that traffic went through blender_python instead of the tools. Call it first when a tool answers unexpectedly.

name: blender_install_addon
description: Builds the add-on zip in the data directory and returns the path with the steps to install it in Blender (Preferences → Get Extensions → Install from Disk). Needed once per Blender installation and whenever blender_diagnose reports that the installed add-on differs from the one this server ships. Over HTTP the add-on comes with the Blender image beside this server, so a mismatch is fixed with the image rather than with this zip.

name: blender_skills

name: blender_enable_skill
description: Loads a skill: its tools appear in the tool list right away (the client is notified). A skill stays loaded until blender_disable_skill, unless this server is configured to unload idle ones.

name.description: Skill name as blender_skills lists it.

name: blender_disable_skill
description: Unloads a skill, removing its tools from the tool list.

name.description: Skill name as blender_skills lists it.

name: find_tool
description: Finds the tools for a task. Ask in plain English words for what you are about to do ("bevel the edges", "warm key light", "render four frames in the background"); the answer names the tools with their descriptions, the skill each belongs to, the command each sends and every parameter it takes. That is enough to call them at once through run_program, which needs no skill loaded; pass enable to put the tools themselves in the tool list instead. Most of this server's tools are not in the tool list until their skill is enabled, so a tool you cannot see is not a tool that does not exist: ask here before reaching for blender_python.

intent.description: What you are trying to do, in English words: "bevel the edges of a mesh", "warm key light on the subject", "render four frames in the background".

limit.description: Most tools to return, 1 to 25; 8 by default.

enable.description: Load the skills the matches live in, so their tools join the tool list; false by default, because the answer already carries what it takes to call them through run_program.

name: run_program
description: Runs a small JavaScript program that calls the commands itself: blender.add_primitive({kind: "cube", name: "Crate"}) and so on for every command of the catalog, with loops, conditions and the results in hand. Use it when a build takes many steps, when each step depends on what the last one answered, or when only a summary of a long listing matters: the steps run here, and only what the program returns comes back, instead of one call and one reply per step. Return a value from the program; log(...) adds a line to the reply. A failed command throws {type, message, details}, which the program may catch and carry on. This is not Blender's Python: the program reaches nothing but the commands, and blender_python stays the last resort for what no command does. The reply lists every command it sent. Limits: 200 commands, the timeout it was given, and one program's memory.

code.description: JavaScript. Call commands as blender.<command>({...}) — the names find_tool reports, the tool name without blender_ — return a value, log(...) to add a line. Up to 200 commands, no files, no network, no bpy.

input.description: Values the program reads as input, e.g. {"count": 8}.

timeoutSeconds.description: Seconds to wait for Blender, 1 to 600.

name: run_tools
description: Runs a list of bridge commands in this Blender, in order, in one call: what to use for a build that takes many steps. A step is a command name and its params — the tool name without blender_, so add_primitive, transform_object, create_material — with the params named as the add-on reads them, the tool's parameter names in snake_case: adaptive_threshold, not adaptiveThreshold. A key the command does not read fails the step as BadRequest, naming the key it was probably meant to be, rather than vanishing from it. Each step passes the add-on's own checks, the same lease guard and the same journal as a direct tool call. Generate the list with a loop instead of writing a script: this, not blender_python, is what makes repetitive building cheap. Stops at the first failed step unless told to continue, and returns every step that ran with its result or its error; up to 500 steps, whose results are dropped from the reply once it grows past half a megabyte, each dropped one marked omitted.

commands.description: Steps in order: [{"command": "add_primitive", "params": {"kind": "cube", "name": "Crate"}}, ...]; command names are the bridge names, the tool name without blender_. Up to 500 steps.

continueOnError.description: Keep going after a failed step; either way the reply lists every step that ran with its result or its error.

timeoutSeconds.description: Seconds to wait for Blender, 1 to 600.

name: blender_upload
description: Copies a file, or every file under a folder, from this machine to the machine Blender runs on: textures, HDRIs, models and .blend files a remote Blender cannot otherwise see. A relative localPath is read from the project — the folder the client works in — and without a remotePath the file lands in the project's twin on Blender's machine at the same relative path, so the two folders mirror each other; blender_diagnose names both under project. Sent in chunks and checked by SHA-256 before the file takes its name; an existing file is kept unless overwrite. With Blender on this same machine none of this is needed. Over HTTP the call copies nothing itself: remotePath is required, relative to the files area and starting with the project's folder (robot/textures), and the reply holds a command to run in a shell on the client's machine, from the folder you work in, before expires; it sends the file in parts of 16 MB, a folder as one tar, checked by SHA-256 at the end.

localPath.description: File or folder on this machine: absolute, or relative to the project, the folder the client works in.

remotePath.description: Where it lands on Blender's machine: absolute, or relative to the add-on's files folder; the same relative path in the project's twin otherwise.

overwrite.description: Replace files that already exist there.

name: blender_download
description: Copies a file, or every file under a folder, from the machine Blender runs on to this one: finished frames, render job output, saved .blend files. Without a localPath it lands in the project — the folder the client works in — at the relative path it had in the project's twin over there, or under its own name when it came from elsewhere; with no project, in the downloads folder of this server's data directory. Checked by SHA-256 before the file takes its name, and an existing local file is kept unless overwrite. Over HTTP the call copies nothing itself: remotePath must be relative to the files area and start with the project's folder, and the reply holds a command to run in a shell on the client's machine, from the folder you work in, before expires; it writes to localPath or to the same relative place without the project's folder and keeps files that exist unless overwrite, while the server checks every file against the SHA-256 the add-on computed and breaks the command off when one differs.

remotePath.description: File or folder on Blender's machine: absolute, or relative to the add-on's files folder.

localPath.description: Where it lands on this machine: absolute, or relative to the project; the matching place in the project otherwise.

overwrite.description: Replace local files that already exist.

Prefer the dedicated tools when one exists.

name: blender_python
description: Runs Python inside Blender with bpy available and returns stdout plus the value assigned to result. The last resort, and there is a procedure before it: find_tool for what you are about to do, run_tools for a build of many steps, blender_run_operator for a single operator. What a script does passes no validation, ignores the leases other agents hold and lands in the journal as unguarded, so nobody can see which objects it touched; the reply names the tools that already cover what it did. Blender's Python API is fully reachable, which is what this is for: what no tool of this server does.

baseColor.description: [r, g, b] or [r, g, b, a] with components 0 to 1.

alpha.description: Opacity 0 to 1; below 1 needs a blend method.

blendMethod.description: How alpha renders: OPAQUE, CLIP, HASHED, BLEND.

inputs.description: Unlinked input sockets by name, e.g. {"Scale": 5, "Base Color": [1, 0, 0]}.

properties.description: Non-socket settings by Python name, e.g. {"noise_dimensions": "4D"}, {"blend_type": "MULTIPLY"}, {"operation": "ADD"}.

name: blender_remove_node

material.description: Material name as blender_list_materials shows it.

node.description: Node name as blender_material_info lists it, e.g. Principled BSDF.

material.description: Material name as blender_list_materials shows it.

channels.description: Animated properties: location, rotation_euler, scale, or any data path such as data.energy for a light, data.lens for a camera, hide_render.

scene.description: Scene to act on; the current scene otherwise.

preview.description: Return a small JPEG of the result as image content, with exposure statistics; false for the path only.

timeoutSeconds.description: Seconds to wait for Blender, 1 to 600.

note.description: Free text, e.g. the version; switches the note field on.

region.description: Render region [minX, minY, maxX, maxY] as fractions of the frame, 0 to 1; pass null to render the whole frame.

cropToRegion.description: Crop the output to the region instead of leaving the rest empty.

preset.description: Resolution preset, which also sets the percentage to 100: HD, FHD, QHD, UHD, 8K, DCI_2K, DCI_4K, SQUARE_1K, SQUARE_2K, PORTRAIT_FHD, PORTRAIT_UHD, CINEMASCOPE_2K, CINEMASCOPE_4K.

mode.description: STEREO_3D (left and right eye) or MULTIVIEW (any number of cameras).

format.description: File layout: INDIVIDUAL files per view or STEREO_3D packed (anaglyph, interlace, side by side).

convergenceDistance.description: Distance in metres where the eyes converge.

interocularDistance.description: Distance between the eyes in metres; 0.065 is human.

pivot.description: CENTER, LEFT or RIGHT: which eye the camera object stands for.

scene.description: Scene to act on; the current scene otherwise.

name: blender_set_cycles
description: Switches to Cycles and sets its sampling in depth: samples, adaptive sampling with threshold and minimum, a time limit, the denoiser with prefilter, passes and quality, GPU denoising, device and compute backend (CUDA, OptiX, HIP, oneAPI, Metal) with the devices this machine has, light paths per bounce type, caustics, clamping, light tree, seed and persistent data; anything else by Python name.

activate.description: Switch the scene to Cycles; false only changes the settings.

samples.description: Maximum samples per pixel; 64 to 256 for previews, 1024 to 4096 for finals with adaptive sampling.

adaptiveSampling.description: Adaptive sampling on or off; it stops sampling pixels that converged.

adaptiveThreshold.description: Noise threshold for adaptive sampling; 0.01 is the default, 0.001 cleaner and slower.

adaptiveMinSamples.description: Minimum samples before adaptive sampling may stop; 0 lets Blender choose.

timeLimit.description: Seconds per frame after which sampling stops; 0 is no limit.

denoiser.description: OPENIMAGEDENOISE (every platform) or OPTIX (NVIDIA only); the reply lists what this machine has.

denoisePrefilter.description: Denoiser prefilter: ACCURATE (the default), FAST or NONE.

denoisePasses.description: Passes the denoiser uses: RGB, RGB_ALBEDO or RGB_ALBEDO_NORMAL (the default, best).

denoiseQuality.description: Denoiser quality: HIGH, BALANCED or FAST.

denoiseGpu.description: Run the denoiser on the GPU.

device.description: CPU or GPU; GPU needs a compute backend, which backend sets.

backend.description: Compute backend for GPU rendering: OPTIX or CUDA (NVIDIA), HIP (AMD), ONEAPI (Intel), METAL (Apple), NONE for the CPU alone. Enables every device of that backend and sets the device to GPU; the reply lists the devices this machine has, and render jobs take the choice to their worker.

transparent.description: Transparent bounces; raise for leaves and hair with alpha.

caustics.description: Caustics; off with glossy blur reduces fireflies.

blurGlossy.description: Blur glossy reflections after blurry bounces to kill fireflies; 1 is the default.

clamp.description: Clamp sample brightness; 0 is no clamp.

indirect.description: Clamp indirect light; 10 removes fireflies with little energy loss.

seed.description: Noise seed; animatedSeed changes it per frame.

animatedSeed.description: Change the seed every frame so noise does not stick in animations.

persistentData.description: Keep scene data between frames; faster animations, more memory.

settings.description: Any other scene.cycles setting by Python name, e.g. {"use_guiding": true, "volume_step_rate": 0.5, "texture_limit_render": "2048"}.

scene.description: Scene to act on; the current scene otherwise.

name: blender_set_eevee
description: Switches to EEVEE and sets its quality: samples, shadows with rays, steps and resolution, ray tracing with its options, fast GI, volumetrics, clamping, depth-of-field bokeh, overscan and high quality normals; anything else by Python name.

activate.description: Switch the scene to EEVEE; false only changes the settings.

samples.description: Render samples; 64 is the default, 16 for previews, 256 and up for clean soft shadows.

shadowRays.description: Shadow rays per sample, 1 to 16; more is smoother.

raytracing.description: Screen-space ray tracing for reflections and refractions.

maxRoughness.description: Roughness above which reflections fall back to probes.

thickness.description: Surface thickness assumed by the screen trace.

fastGi.description: Fast global illumination approximation for rough surfaces.

tileSize.description: "2", "4", "8" or "16"; smaller is finer and slower.

distribution.description: Sample distribution 0 to 1; higher packs samples near the camera.

clamp.description: Clamp light per surface and volume.

overscan.description: Render a margin outside the frame so screen-space effects do not fade at the edges.

overscanSize.description: Overscan size in percent of the frame, 0 to 50.

highQualityNormals.description: High quality normals for smooth shading.

settings.description: Any other scene.eevee setting by Python name, e.g. {"use_taa_reprojection": true, "shadow_pool_size": "1024"}.

scene.description: Scene to act on; the current scene otherwise.

name: blender_set_motion_blur
description: Sets motion blur for renders: on or off, shutter time in frames, shutter position, Cycles rolling shutter, EEVEE steps and maximum blur, and whether the view layers use it.

shutter.description: Shutter time in frames; 0.5 is a 180° shutter, the film look.

position.description: Where the shutter opens relative to the frame: START, CENTER (the default) or END.

rollingShutterDuration.description: Cycles rolling shutter duration as a fraction of the frame, 0 to 1.

steps.description: EEVEE motion steps, 1 and up; more steps blur curved motion correctly.

depthScale.description: EEVEE depth scale that separates foreground from background blur.

viewLayerEnabled.description: Apply motion blur on every view layer of the scene, or not.

shutterCurve.description: Shutter opening over the exposure as [[t, open], ...] from t 0 to 1; [[0,0],[0.1,1],[0.9,1],[1,0]] imitates a mechanical shutter, a flat 1 is the default.

scene.description: Scene to act on; the current scene otherwise.

name: blender_set_freestyle
description: Freestyle line rendering: on or off, line thickness and mode, crease angle, and line sets with their edge types, visibility, colour and thickness; for toon, technical and ink looks.

enabled.description: Freestyle on or off for the scene and view layer.

thicknessMode.description: ABSOLUTE or RELATIVE to the resolution.

creaseAngle.description: Angle in degrees above which an edge counts as a crease.

linesets.description: Line sets to create or update.

name.description: Line set name; LineSet is Blender's default one.

edges.description: Edge types that draw: silhouette, border, crease, contour, external_contour, material_boundary, edge_mark, suggestive_contour, ridge_valley.

viewLayer.description: View layer; the active one otherwise.

scene.description: Scene to act on; the current scene otherwise.

name: blender_view_layer
description: Creates, configures, lists, activates or removes view layers: which collections are excluded, holdout or indirect-only, the render passes, cryptomatte (object, material, asset, levels), AOVs, light groups and their members, material and world overrides, per-layer samples. Returns the layer with its collection tree.

action.description: configure (the default; creates the layer when the name is new), create, activate, list, remove.

name.description: View layer name; the active one otherwise.

use.description: Render this layer; false skips it in renders.

samples.description: Per-layer sample override for Cycles; 0 uses the scene samples.

collections.description: Which collections the layer renders, holds out or keeps for bounce light only.

include.description: Collections rendered normally; also clears holdout and indirect-only on them.

exclude.description: Collections left out of this layer.

holdout.description: Collections cut as transparent holes, for plates.

indirectOnly.description: Collections that only contribute bounce light and reflections.

reset.description: Clear every exclusion, holdout and indirect-only first.

passes.description: Passes to switch: {"z": true, "normal": true, "mist": true, "vector": true, "ambient_occlusion": true, "diffuse_direct": true, "shadow_catcher": true, "cryptomatte_object": true}.

levels.description: Levels, an even number 2 to 16; 6 keeps three overlapping objects per pixel.

aovs.description: AOVs to create or keep: ["Mask"] or [{"name": "Wetness", "type": "VALUE"}]; shaders write them through an AOV Output node.

lightGroups.description: Light groups to create: ["Key", "Fill", "Rim"]; each renders as its own Combined pass.

lightGroupMembers.description: Which lights belong to which group: {"Key": ["Sun"], "Fill": ["Area", "World"]}.

materialOverride.description: Material name that overrides every material on this layer (clay renders); empty removes it.

freestyle.description: Render the layer with Freestyle lines.

scene.description: Scene to act on; the current scene otherwise.

name: blender_light_linking
description: Cycles light and shadow linking: which objects or collections a light illuminates (include: only these; exclude: all but these) and which cast its shadow. Returns the receiver and blocker lists with their states.

light.description: The light object (or emissive mesh) whose reach changes.

receivers.description: Objects or collections that receive its light.

receiverMode.description: include: the light reaches only the receivers; exclude: everything except them.

blockers.description: Objects or collections that cast its shadow.

blockerMode.description: include: only the blockers cast this light's shadow; exclude: everything except them.

clear.description: Remove the light's receiver and blocker collections first.

name: blender_set_camera_optics
description: The physical camera: sensor size and fit, focal length or field of view, lens shift, clip range, perspective, orthographic or panoramic type, aperture with f-stop, blade count, rotation and anamorphic ratio, focus by distance, object or bone. Returns the optics and the hyperfocal distance. Motion blur lives in blender_set_motion_blur and, per object, in blender_object_render_flags.

camera.description: Camera object; the scene camera otherwise.

width.description: Width in mm: 36 full frame, 23.5 APS-C, 24.89 Super 35, 6.17 phone.

height.description: Height in mm; 24 for full frame.

fit.description: AUTO, HORIZONTAL or VERTICAL: which sensor edge the field of view follows.

fov.description: Horizontal field of view in degrees instead of the focal length.

shift.description: Lens shift [x, y] as fractions of the frame; keeps verticals parallel without tilting the camera.

type.description: PERSP, ORTHO or PANO.

panorama.description: Panoramic projection, which also sets the type to PANO: EQUIRECTANGULAR, FISHEYE_EQUIDISTANT, FISHEYE_EQUISOLID, FISHEYE_LENS_POLYNOMIAL, CENTRAL_CYLINDRICAL.

aperture.description: Aperture: f-stop, blades, rotation, anamorphic ratio.

enabled.description: Depth of field on or off; on when any other field is given.

blades.description: Iris blades: 0 is a perfect circle, 5 to 9 give polygonal bokeh.

ratio.description: Anamorphic squeeze: 1 spherical, 2 for 2x anamorphic bokeh.

focus.description: Focus by distance, object or bone.

distance.description: Focus distance in metres; cleared when an object is given.

bone.description: Bone of the focus object, e.g. an eye, for rigs.

scene.description: Scene to act on; the current scene otherwise.

name: blender_camera_move
description: Animates a camera move around a subject over a frame range: turntable, orbit, dolly, push-in or crane, with the camera aimed at the subject. Product videos and look-development spins in one call.

type.description: turntable (the subject spins on a pivot under a still camera), orbit (the camera circles the subject), dolly or push_in (the camera moves towards the subject), crane (the camera rises).

camera.description: Camera to move; the scene camera otherwise. Not used by turntable.

start.description: First frame; the scene start otherwise.

end.description: Last frame; the scene end otherwise.

revolutions.description: turntable, orbit: full turns over the range; 1 by default.

startAngle.description: Start angle around the subject in degrees.

distance.description: orbit, dolly, crane: camera distance from the subject in metres; from its size otherwise.

distanceEnd.description: dolly, push_in: distance at the end; half the start otherwise.

height.description: orbit, dolly: camera height above the subject centre; crane: start height.

interpolation.description: LINEAR (the default, for loops) or BEZIER (eases in and out).

pivotName.description: Name of the pivot empty for turntable and orbit.

scene.description: Scene to act on; the current scene otherwise.

name: blender_light_rig
description: Builds a three-point rig of area lights around a subject: key, fill and rim at studio angles, sized and powered from the subject's size, each with a colour temperature and aimed at the subject. Replaces a rig of the same name.

name.description: Name prefix for the lights; Rig otherwise.

roles.description: Lights to build: key, fill, rim; all three otherwise.

keyEnergy.description: Key light power in watts; 1000 by default.

fillRatio.description: Fill power as a fraction of the key; 0.35 by default (a 3:1 ratio).

rimRatio.description: Rim power as a fraction of the key; 1.5 by default.

keyAngle.description: Key light direction around the subject in degrees; 45 by default.

distance.description: Distance of the lights from the subject in metres; from its size otherwise.

keyTemperature.description: Key colour temperature in kelvin; 5600 by default.

fillTemperature.description: Fill colour temperature in kelvin; 6500 by default.

rimTemperature.description: Rim colour temperature in kelvin; 6500 by default.

scene.description: Scene to act on; the current scene otherwise.

name: blender_object_render_flags
description: Per-object rendering flags for integration and passes: holdout, shadow catcher, visibility per ray type, pass index for the object index pass, light group, caustics role, per-object motion blur, shadow terminator offset. Objects or whole collections. Returns each object's effective flags.

names.description: Objects, or collection names to apply to every object inside.

holdout.description: Cut a transparent hole where the object is, for compositing over a plate.

shadowCatcher.description: Render only the shadows and reflections the object receives (Cycles).

passIndex.description: Value written to the IndexOB pass; an ID Mask node in blender_compositor isolates it.

lightGroup.description: Light group for lights and emissive meshes; empty string removes it.

steps.description: Motion steps 1 to 7; more steps blur curved motion correctly.

deform.description: Blur deformation as well as transforms.

shadowTerminatorOffset.description: Shadow terminator offset 0 to 1; hides the shading artefact on low-poly smooth meshes.

name: blender_render_object
description: Renders one object (or a few) alone: a temporary camera frames them from a chosen angle, everything else is hidden from the render, the background is transparent. A product shot in one call.

path.description: Absolute path of the image to write.

name.description: Name of the object as shown in the outliner.

names.description: Several objects to frame together instead of one.

azimuth.description: Camera direction around the vertical axis in degrees; 0 looks from +X.

elevation.description: Camera height angle in degrees; 0 is level, 90 is straight down.

margin.description: Space around the object; 1 fills the frame, 1.15 is the default.

keepCamera.description: Keep the temporary camera (SnailShot) in the scene.

preview.description: Return a small JPEG of the result as image content, with exposure statistics; false for the path only.

timeoutSeconds.description: Seconds to wait for Blender, 1 to 600.

name: blender_viewport_capture
description: Grabs the 3D viewport as the user sees it, in its current shading, to a file; fast feedback without a render. Needs Blender's window.

path.description: Absolute path of the image to write.

preview.description: Return a small JPEG of the result as image content, with exposure statistics; false for the path only.

name: blender_inspect_image
description: Looks at an image file: a preview the model can see, plus exposure statistics (mean luminance, clipped highlights and shadows, a histogram). For frames a background job wrote, textures, or any render on disk.

path.description: Absolute path of the image: PNG, JPEG, EXR, TIFF or anything Blender opens.

preview.description: Return a small JPEG of the result as image content, with exposure statistics; false for the path only.

previewSize.description: Longest edge of the preview in pixels; 512 by default, 1024 to read fine detail.

name: blender_bake_texture
description: Bakes a material channel (colour, normal, AO, roughness, combined) into a PNG through the mesh's UVs with Cycles; the way to take procedural materials into game engines.

name.description: Name of the mesh object.

path.description: Absolute path of the PNG to write.

type.description: DIFFUSE, COMBINED, AO, NORMAL, ROUGHNESS, EMIT, SHADOW, POSITION, UV, GLOSSY, TRANSMISSION or ENVIRONMENT.

width.description: Texture width in pixels, up to 4096.

height.description: Texture height in pixels; the width otherwise.

samples.description: Cycles samples; low values are fine for colour bakes.

margin.description: Pixels of bleed around UV islands.

keepNode.description: Leave the image texture node in the materials.

preview.description: Return a small JPEG of the result as image content, with exposure statistics; false for the path only.

timeoutSeconds.description: Seconds to wait for Blender, 1 to 600.

name: blender_render_job
description: Starts a background render: the file is saved as a copy and a second Blender renders it, so this Blender and the tools stay free. Frames, cameras, view layers, engine, output template with {scene} and {camera} and ####, format and depth. Jobs queue up and run maxParallel at a time, retry on failure, and can split into chunks that render interleaved frames in parallel. Returns the job id; poll blender_render_job_status. Save the file first: unsaved changes are included, but relative paths resolve best from a saved file.

outputPath.description: Output path template: folder and prefix with #### for the frame number, {scene} and {camera} for their names, e.g. /renders/{scene}/{camera}_####. Blender adds the extension; a finished file name such as shot_0001.png is refused, pass shot_####.png.

frames.description: Frames to render: 1-240, every second frame 1-240x2, a list 1,5,9-12; the scene range otherwise.

cameras.description: Cameras to render one after another, each into its own files through {camera}; the scene camera otherwise.

viewLayers.description: View layers to render; every enabled layer otherwise.

engine.description: EEVEE, CYCLES or WORKBENCH; the scene's engine otherwise.

output.description: What the job writes: format, depth, codec, size, samples, overwrite and placeholders.

fileFormat.description: PNG, JPEG, OPEN_EXR, OPEN_EXR_MULTILAYER, TIFF, WEBP or FFMPEG; the scene's format otherwise.

colorDepth.description: Bits per channel: 8 or 16 for PNG and TIFF, 16 (half) or 32 (full float) for EXR, 8, 10 or 12 for video and DPX.

exrCodec.description: EXR compression: ZIP (lossless, the default), PIZ, ZIPS, RLE, PXR24 (lossy for 32-bit), DWAA and DWAB (lossy, small), B44, B44A, HTJ2K or NONE.

samples.description: Samples per pixel for this job only.

overwrite.description: Overwrite frames that exist; false skips them.

placeholder.description: Write placeholders so several machines can share the range.

queue.description: How the job runs: chunks, parallel jobs, retries, priority, threads and OCIO config.

chunks.description: Processes to split the frame range over; each renders every nth frame, so the sequence fills in evenly. 1 keeps one process.

maxParallel.description: Jobs allowed to run at once on this machine; the rest wait in the queue. 1 keeps one GPU to one render.

retries.description: Restarts after a crash before the job counts as failed.

threads.description: CPU threads for the job; 0 uses every core.

ocioConfig.description: OpenColorIO config file the job renders under; the server's configured one otherwise, else Blender's own.

scene.description: Scene to act on; the current scene otherwise.

name: blender_render_job_status
description: Progress of a background render: state, frames done of total, current frame and camera, elapsed and estimated remaining seconds, peak memory, the files written, the error if it failed and the tail of its log. Without an id, lists recent jobs.

id.description: Job id as blender_render_job returned it.

logLines.description: Lines from the end of the job's log to include.

name: blender_render_job_cancel
description: Stops a background render; frames already written stay on disk.

id.description: Job id as blender_render_job returned it.

name: blender_render_check
description: Pre-flight before a long render: camera, writable output and free disk, unsaved file or changes, missing textures and libraries, disabled view layers, frame range, GPU availability, world and lights, codec. Returns ready true or false with the issues by level.

outputPath.description: Output path to check instead of the scene's; a template with #### works.

scene.description: Scene to act on; the current scene otherwise.

name: blender_render_budget
description: What the frame will cost before rendering it: texture memory by size and depth, geometry after modifiers, instances, particles and hair, the Cycles devices and system memory, and a probe that renders the frame twice at low resolution — the pair separates the fixed cost of a frame from the cost that grows with its pixels, and the estimate is their sum for the whole frame. The memory estimate says where it came from: the probe's own peak plus the frame buffer it did not fill, or the textures and geometry when no probe ran. Verdict fits, tight or exceeds against a memory limit, with recommendations that can be applied in the same call: texture limit, simplify, tile size, device. Optionally packs external files and saves a copy for a farm.

probe.description: Probe render at low resolution to time the frame and measure peak memory; omit to skip.

enabled.description: Off skips the probe; on when any other field is given.

percentage.description: Resolution percentage of the probe, 1 to 50; 10 by default.

samples.description: Samples for the probe; the scene's otherwise.

textureLimit.description: Largest texture edge at render time: OFF, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096 or 8192.

subdivision.description: Maximum subdivision level at render time.

childParticles.description: Fraction of child particles rendered, 0 to 1.

tileSize.description: Cycles tile size in pixels; smaller lowers peak memory.

device.description: CPU, or a device name or type from the reply's devices list.

packForFarm.description: Prepare the file for a farm.

packExternal.description: Pack external images and files into the .blend.

relativePaths.description: Make every path relative to the file; needs a saved file.

copyTo.description: Absolute path for a self-contained copy.

memoryLimitMb.description: Memory the render may use in MB; 80 percent of what this machine, or the container Blender runs in, allows it otherwise.

scene.description: Scene to act on; the current scene otherwise.

timeoutSeconds.description: Seconds to wait for Blender, 1 to 600.

name: blender_lens_effects
description: Rebuilds the post stack on the beauty pass in a compositor's order: denoise (with the denoising data passes), depth of field or motion blur from passes, glare, halation, chromatic aberration, vignette, film grain weighted by luminance and animated per frame, in display space. Each block optional, but at least one is asked for: a call naming none is refused rather than read as clear. A repeated call replaces the stack, clear removes it and wires Render Layers straight to the output. To see the chain that is there, read it with blender_compositor and action info. Data passes stay raw for blender_file_output. Returns the chain and warnings.

denoise.description: Denoise node at the head of the stack.

enabled.description: Off removes the block; on when any other field is given.

useDataPasses.description: Feed albedo and normal from the Cycles denoising data pass and switch Cycles' own denoising off; the studio way.

hdr.description: Treat the image as HDR; on by default.

defocus.description: Depth of field from the Z pass.

fstop.description: f-number of the simulated lens; lower blurs more.

bokeh.description: CIRCLE, TRIANGLE, SQUARE, PENTAGON, HEXAGON, HEPTAGON or OCTAGON.

zScale.description: Scale of the Z values; 1 for metres.

vectorBlur.description: Motion blur from the Vector pass; scene motion blur must be off.

samples.description: Samples along the motion; 32 is smooth.

shutter.description: Shutter time in frames; 0.5 is a 180° shutter.

type.description: BLOOM, GHOSTS, STREAKS, FOG_GLOW, SIMPLE_STAR or SUN_BEAMS.

threshold.description: Scene-linear value above which pixels glow; 1 is display white.

strength.description: Mix of the glare over the image, 0 to 1; 0.1 is subtle.

saturation.description: Saturation of the glare; 1 keeps the source colour.

size.description: Spread of the glare; bloom 4 to 9, streaks in pixels.

fade.description: Fade of streaks along their length.

halation.description: Halation, the red halo of film around highlights.

threshold.description: Scene-linear value above which the halo forms.

strength.description: Mix of the halo, 0 to 1; 0.15 is film.

tint.description: Halo colour [r, g, b]; warm red by default.

dispersion.description: Colour fringing 0 to 1; 0.02 subtle, 0.1 a cheap lens.

fit.description: Scale to keep the frame filled.

roundness.description: 1 is an ellipse matching the frame, below 1 rounder.

grain.description: Film grain, animated and weighted by luminance.

strength.description: Amount 0 to 1; 0.05 to 0.15 reads as film.

size.description: Grain size in pixels at output resolution; 1.5 for 35 mm at 4K.

chroma.description: 0 monochrome grain, 1 full colour grain; 0.3 by default.

animated.description: A new pattern every frame; on by default.

space.description: DISPLAY adds the grain after the view transform so clipped highlights stay clean; LINEAR before it.

shadows.description: Weight in the shadows; 0.6 by default.

midtones.description: Weight in the midtones; 1 by default.

highlights.description: Weight in the highlights; 0.2 by default.

clear.description: Remove the stack and wire Render Layers straight to the output; the only way to take it down, since a call naming no effect is refused.

scene.description: Scene to act on; the current scene otherwise.

name: blender_compositor
description: Reads or edits the compositor by hand: list nodes, reset to Render Layers → output, add a node with inputs and settings, link sockets, remove a node. Render passes appear as outputs of the Render Layers node. Grain, glare and the rest of the post stack come from blender_lens_effects. Applies to every render from then on.

action.description: info (list nodes and links), clear (reset to Render Layers → output), add_node, link, remove_node.

type.description: add_node: compositor node bl_idname or suffix: Blur, Glare, Filter, ColorBalance, HueSat, BrightContrast, Denoise, Lensdist, Defocus, Kuwahara, AlphaOver, Viewer, OutputFile, RLayers; Mix, Math and Noise from the shader set; Composite is the output.

name.description: add_node: name for the node; remove_node: node to delete.

inputs.description: add_node: input sockets by name, e.g. {"Size": 10}; menu sockets take their label, e.g. Filter {"Type": "Box Sharpen"}.

properties.description: add_node: settings by Python name, e.g. {"filter_type": "GAUSS"}, {"glare_type": "FOG_GLOW"}.

location.description: add_node: [x, y] position in the editor.

fromSocket.description: link: output socket on the source, e.g. Image, Depth, Normal.

toSocket.description: link: input socket on the target.

name: blender_file_output
description: Configures a File Output node in the compositor: a folder, a format with its depth and codec, and one slot per render pass wired from the Render Layers node, each with an optional format of its own. Passes that are off get switched on. A multilayer EXR keeps every slot in one file; other formats write one file per slot.

action.description: configure (create or update the node), info (list File Output nodes), remove.

name.description: Node name; File Output otherwise. Several nodes write to several places.

directory.description: Absolute folder the files go to.

fileName.description: File name prefix before the slot name and frame number, e.g. shot01_.

fileFormat.description: OPEN_EXR_MULTILAYER (every slot in one file), OPEN_EXR, PNG, JPEG, TIFF, WEBP, DPX.

colorDepth.description: Bits per channel: 8 or 16 for PNG and TIFF, 16 (half) or 32 (full float) for EXR, 8, 10 or 12 for video and DPX.

exrCodec.description: EXR compression: ZIP (lossless, the default), PIZ, ZIPS, RLE, PXR24 (lossy for 32-bit), DWAA and DWAB (lossy, small), B44, B44A, HTJ2K or NONE.

slots.description: Slots, one per pass, replacing the current ones: pass names such as Image, Depth, Normal, Mist, AO, Vector, Position, UV, Emit, Env, Shadow, IndexOB, CryptoObject00, or objects {"pass": "Depth", "name": "Z", "file_format": "OPEN_EXR", "color_depth": 32, "save_as_render": false}; save_as_render applies the view transform, off for data passes and for EXR unless asked.

allPasses.description: One slot for every pass the Render Layers node offers.

name: blender_cryptomatte_matte
description: Adds a Cryptomatte node that mattes the named objects, materials or assets, switching the cryptomatte pass on, and optionally writes the matte through a File Output slot. Its Matte output isolates them for grading or replacement.

names.description: Objects, materials or assets to matte, by name.

layer.description: object (the default), material or asset: which cryptomatte layer the names live in.

name.description: Name for the Cryptomatte node; derived from the names otherwise.

output.description: File Output node to write the matte through; created when missing.

directory.description: Folder for that File Output node.

slot.description: Slot name in the File Output node; Matte otherwise.

scene.description: Scene to act on; the current scene otherwise.

name: blender_import_file
description: Imports a model or scene file into the current scene and lists the objects it added; the format follows the extension.

path.description: Absolute path of the file to import.

format.description: Format when the extension does not say: fbx, obj, stl, ply, gltf, glb, dae, usd, usda, usdc, usdz, abc, x3d, svg, dxf, 3ds.

options.description: Extra importer properties by name, as blender_describe_operator lists them for the importer, e.g. {"global_scale": 0.01}.

timeoutSeconds.description: Seconds to wait for Blender, 1 to 600.

name: blender_export_file
description: Exports the scene or the selected objects to a file; the format follows the extension. glb packs everything into one file.

path.description: Absolute path of the file to write; folders are created.

format.description: Format when the extension does not say: fbx, obj, stl, ply, gltf, glb, dae, usd, usda, usdc, usdz, abc, x3d, dxf, 3ds.

selectedOnly.description: Export only selected objects instead of the whole scene.

names.description: With selectedOnly: select exactly these objects first.

options.description: Extra exporter properties by name, e.g. {"apply_unit_scale": true}, {"export_apply": true}.

timeoutSeconds.description: Seconds to wait for Blender, 1 to 600.

name: blender_list_assets
description: Lists what another .blend file holds by type: objects, collections, materials, node groups, worlds, images and more.

types.description: Types to list: objects, collections, materials, node_groups, worlds, images, meshes, actions, cameras, lights, scenes, texts; every type otherwise.

name: blender_append_assets
description: Appends (copies) or links objects, collections, materials, node groups, worlds or images from another .blend file into the scene, optionally into a collection; linked collections arrive as instances.

type.description: objects (the default), collections, materials, node_groups, worlds, images, meshes, actions, cameras, lights.

names.description: Names to bring in; everything of that type otherwise.

link.description: Link instead of append: the data stays in the other file and updates with it.

collection.description: Collection to place objects or collections into; created when missing.

scene.description: Scene to act on; the current scene otherwise.

name: blender_sequencer_info
description: The timeline: every strip with its channel, frames, trims, blend and source, plus the frame range, fps, resolution and output format.

name: blender_sequencer_add_strip
description: Adds a strip to the timeline: a movie (with its sound), an image or an image sequence from a folder or file list, a sound file, a 3D scene, a solid colour or a text title, placed on a channel from a frame, with optional fades, transform and blend.

type.description: movie, image, sound, scene (renders a 3D scene into the timeline), color or text.

name.description: Name for the strip.

path.description: movie, image, sound: absolute path of the file.

scene.description: scene: name of the scene to render into the strip; the current scene otherwise.

channel.description: Timeline channel (row), 1 and up; the first free one otherwise.

frameStart.description: Frame the strip starts on; the scene start otherwise.

length.description: color, text, image: length in frames.

color.description: color: [r, g, b]; text: [r, g, b] or [r, g, b, a].

location.description: text: [x, y] position, 0 to 1 from the bottom-left.

withSound.description: movie: also add its audio as a sound strip on the next channel.

blendType.description: How the strip mixes with the channels below: REPLACE, ALPHA_OVER (the default for effects), CROSS, ADD, MULTIPLY, SCREEN, OVERLAY, DIFFERENCE and the other blend modes.

transform.description: Picture placement: offset, scale, rotation, crop and flip.

crop.description: [left, right, bottom, top] crop in pixels.

fade.description: Fades in frames; opacity for pictures, volume for sound.

settings.description: Further strip properties by Python name, e.g. text {"use_box": true, "wrap_width": 0.8}, SPEED {"speed_factor": 2}, WIPE {"transition_type": "CLOCK"}, GAUSSIAN_BLUR {"size_x": 20, "size_y": 20}, GLOW {"threshold": 0.5}.

name: blender_sequencer_add_effect
description: Adds a transition or effect strip: a cross-fade or wipe between two strips where they overlap, a blur, glow or speed change on one, or a generated colour or text.

type.description: Transitions between two strips: CROSS, GAMMA_CROSS, WIPE; mixes of two: ADD, SUBTRACT, MULTIPLY, ALPHA_OVER, ALPHA_UNDER, COLORMIX; on one strip: GLOW, GAUSSIAN_BLUR, SPEED, ADJUSTMENT; generators: COLOR, TEXT; special: MULTICAM, COMPOSITOR.

inputs.description: Input strip names: two for transitions and mixes, one for GLOW, GAUSSIAN_BLUR, SPEED and ADJUSTMENT, none for COLOR and TEXT.

name.description: Name for the effect strip.

channel.description: Timeline channel; the first free one otherwise.

frameStart.description: Start frame; where the inputs overlap otherwise.

length.description: Length in frames; the overlap of the inputs otherwise.

settings.description: Further strip properties by Python name, e.g. text {"use_box": true, "wrap_width": 0.8}, SPEED {"speed_factor": 2}, WIPE {"transition_type": "CLOCK"}, GAUSSIAN_BLUR {"size_x": 20, "size_y": 20}, GLOW {"threshold": 0.5}.

name: blender_sequencer_update_strip
description: Moves, trims, mutes, fades, re-blends, transforms or renames a strip; changes text, colour or volume.

name.description: Strip name as blender_sequencer_info lists it.

frameStart.description: Move the strip to start on this frame.

length.description: New length in frames (for images, colours, text and effects).

trimStart.description: Frames cut from the beginning of the source.

trimEnd.description: Frames cut from the end of the source.

blendType.description: How the strip mixes with the channels below: REPLACE, ALPHA_OVER (the default for effects), CROSS, ADD, MULTIPLY, SCREEN, OVERLAY, DIFFERENCE and the other blend modes.

volume.description: sound: volume, 1 is the source level.

transform.description: Picture placement: offset, scale, rotation, crop and flip.

crop.description: [left, right, bottom, top] crop in pixels.

fade.description: Fades in frames; opacity for pictures, volume for sound.

settings.description: Further strip properties by Python name, e.g. text {"use_box": true, "wrap_width": 0.8}, SPEED {"speed_factor": 2}, WIPE {"transition_type": "CLOCK"}, GAUSSIAN_BLUR {"size_x": 20, "size_y": 20}, GLOW {"threshold": 0.5}.

name: blender_sequencer_remove_strip
description: Removes one strip, or every strip with all=true.

name.description: Strip to remove.

all.description: Remove every strip and start over.

name: blender_sequencer_render
description: Encodes the timeline to a video file with FFmpeg: container by extension, codec, quality and audio codec, or whatever blender_sequencer_encode prepared. The frame range is fitted to the strips unless given. Long for big timelines: set a timeout that fits.

path.description: Absolute path of the video to write; the extension picks the container: .mp4, .mkv, .webm, .mov, .avi, .ogv.

codec.description: H264 (the default), H265, AV1, WEBM (VP9), DNXHD, FFV1 and the rest FFmpeg offers.

quality.description: LOSSLESS, PERC_LOSSLESS, HIGH, MEDIUM (the default), LOW, VERYLOW, LOWEST.

audioCodec.description: AAC (the default), MP3, VORBIS, OPUS, FLAC, PCM or NONE.

fitRange.description: Set the frame range to cover every strip before encoding.

start.description: First frame to encode; overrides fitRange.

end.description: Last frame to encode; overrides fitRange.

timeoutSeconds.description: Seconds to wait for Blender, 1 to 600.

name: blender_sequencer_split
description: Cuts a strip at a frame into two strips on the same channel, keeping both or one side; movie, sound, image, scene, colour and text strips. Effects and transitions are cut by cutting their inputs.

name.description: Strip to cut, as blender_sequencer_info lists it.

frame.description: Frame where the cut goes; the right part starts on it.

keep.description: both (the default), left or right: which parts stay.

rightName.description: Name for the right part; the strip's name plus .R otherwise.

name: blender_sequencer_proxy
description: Sets up proxies (25, 50, 75, 100 percent) for smooth playback of heavy footage, per strip or for all, with optional project-level storage, and builds them when the Video Sequencer editor is open in Blender.

names.description: Strips to set up; every movie and image strip with all=true.

all.description: Every strip instead of a list.

sizes.description: Proxy sizes in percent: 25, 50, 75, 100; [25] is the default and enough for editing.

quality.description: JPEG quality of the proxies, 1 to 100.

directory.description: Project folder for the proxies instead of next to each source.

build.description: Build the proxies now; needs the Video Sequencer editor open in Blender, otherwise only the settings are stored.

enabled.description: Use proxies on these strips, or stop using them.

name: blender_sequencer_timing
description: Sets the project timing: frame rate including fractional rates (23.976, 29.97, 59.94), sync mode for playback (audio sync, frame drop), pixel aspect, resolution and the frame range.

fps.description: Frames per second; 23.976, 29.97 and 59.94 become the matching fractional rates.

syncMode.description: NONE, FRAME_DROP (skip frames to keep time) or AUDIO_SYNC (follow the audio clock) for playback.

pixelAspect.description: Pixel aspect [x, y]; [1, 1] for square pixels.

name: blender_sequencer_grade
description: Grades a strip with modifiers: colour balance (lift/gamma/gain or offset/power/slope), curves by channel, hue correct, brightness and contrast, white balance, tonemap, optionally masked by another strip; lists, updates or removes them.

name.description: Strip to grade.

type.description: COLOR_BALANCE (lift/gamma/gain or offset/power/slope), CURVES, HUE_CORRECT, BRIGHT_CONTRAST, WHITE_BALANCE, TONEMAP, MASK; for sound strips SOUND_EQUALIZER, PITCH, ECHO.

modifier.description: Modifier name to update, or to give a new one; the type's name otherwise.

curves.description: CURVES: points per channel {"C": [[0, 0], [0.25, 0.2], [0.75, 0.8], [1, 1]], "R": [...]}; HUE_CORRECT uses H, S, V.

settings.description: Other modifier settings by Python name: BRIGHT_CONTRAST {"bright": 5, "contrast": 10}, WHITE_BALANCE {"white_value": [r, g, b]}, TONEMAP {"tonemap_type": "RD_PHOTORECEPTOR", "intensity": 0}.

maskStrip.description: Strip whose picture masks the modifier.

clear.description: Remove every modifier from the strip.

name: blender_sequencer_meta
description: Groups strips into a meta strip, or separates one, through Blender's own operators; needs the Video Sequencer editor open in Blender.

action.description: make (the default) groups the named strips; separate unpacks the named meta strip.

names.description: Strips to group, or the meta strip to separate.

newName.description: make: name for the meta strip.

name: blender_sequencer_encode
description: Sets the encode without rendering: container, codec (H264, H265, AV1, ProRes with profile, DNxHD, FFV1, WebM), quality by constant rate factor or a target bitrate with limits, GOP, B-frames, encoder preset, colour depth and audio codec, bitrate, sample rate and channels. blender_sequencer_render then uses these settings.

container.description: mp4, mkv, webm, mov, avi or ogv; the extension of the render path can also decide.

codec.description: H264, H265, AV1, WEBM (VP9), PRORES, DNXHD, FFV1 (lossless), HUFFYUV, MPEG4, THEORA, PNG, QTRLE.

proresProfile.description: ProRes profile, which also selects the PRORES codec: 422_PROXY, 422_LT, 422_STD, 422_HQ, 4444 or 4444_XQ.

quality.description: LOSSLESS, PERC_LOSSLESS, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, VERYLOW, LOWEST; constant quality instead of a bitrate.

crf.description: Exact constant rate factor 0 to 51 for H.264/H.265/AV1; 18 is visually lossless, 23 the default.

bitrate.description: Target bitrate in kbit/s; switches rate control from quality to bitrate.

gop.description: Keyframe interval in frames; smaller seeks better, larger compresses better.

preset.description: Encoder speed preset: BEST (slowest, smallest), GOOD or REALTIME.

lossless.description: Lossless output for codecs that support it.

colorDepth.description: 8, 10 or 12 bits per channel for codecs that support it.

audio.description: Audio codec, bitrate, sample rate and channels.

codec.description: AAC, MP3, VORBIS, OPUS, FLAC, PCM, AC3 or NONE.

sampleRate.description: Sample rate in Hz; 48000 for video.

channels.description: MONO, STEREO, STEREO_LFE, SURROUND4, SURROUND5, SURROUND51, SURROUND61 or SURROUND71.

name: blender_sequencer_mixdown
description: Mixes every sound strip of the timeline down to one audio file: WAV, FLAC, MP3, OGG, AAC or AC3, with sample format, bitrate and channel layout.

path.description: Absolute path of the audio file; the extension picks the container: .wav, .flac, .mp3, .ogg, .aac, .ac3.

codec.description: PCM, FLAC, MP3, VORBIS, AAC, AC3 or MP2; the container's natural codec otherwise.

format.description: Sample format: U8, S16, S24, S32, F32 or F64; F32 for WAV, S16 otherwise.

bitrate.description: Bitrate in kbit/s for lossy codecs; 192 is the default.

channels.description: MONO, STEREO, STEREO_LFE, SURROUND4, SURROUND5, SURROUND51, SURROUND61 or SURROUND71.

splitChannels.description: Write each channel to its own file.

timeoutSeconds.description: Seconds to wait for Blender, 1 to 600.
